meta.description: Apply scoup.ai brand to site and app

user.t: Builder run for REQ-20261009-scoup-brand (this prompt + request.md is your spec). Run dir: C:/Users/mariu/.[REDACTED:high_entropy]. USER DECISIONS: the company is scoup.ai and it is ONE BRAND: "scoup.ai" replaces the product name "Freight Recovery" everywhere a user sees the name. Logo = Concept 3 "Reconciled s". Assets: C:[REDACTED:high_entropy] (13 SVGs) — usage rules (clear space, min sizes, palette, do/don't) are in ../preview.html and the designer notes below. WORKSPACE: do NOT use C:/Users/mariu/ventures/freight-recovery-build (another builder is working there on feat/four-eyes) and do not touch the main checkout C:/Users/mariu/ventures/freight-recovery except git worktree metadata. Create a new worktree: `git -C C:/Users/mariu/ventures/freight-recovery-build worktree add C:/Users/mariu/ventures/freight-recovery-brand -b feat/scoup-brand ae556ab`. Install deps there with `npm ci --ignore-scripts` only if needed for tests (check [SENSITIVE_PATH]; root has verify:no-install-scripts). Use Node 22 at C:[REDACTED:high_entropy].23.3-win-x64. DO: 1. Brand assets: add `brand/` at repo root with all 13 concept-3 SVGs + `brand/README.md` (+ `.no.md` twin) = brand guidelines: name rules, logo files and when to use each, clear space (1x x-height around lockups; 0.25 x tile width around the tile), minimum sizes (horizontal lockup 20px tall / 6mm print; stacked 48px; favicon.svg 16-24px, mark.svg 24px+), palette with contrast ratios (ink #0f172a, teal #0f766e, muted #64748b for ".ai"; on dark: #e2e8f0, #2dd4bf, #8b9ab0; dark tile on light backgrounds, light tile on dark), do/don't (don't offset the halves, don't put dark tile on dark slate, don't swap half colours, don't use the s without its tile in colour versions, don't recolour, stretch, add effects or animate). Note the production TODO: convert stroked lettering to outlines in a vector editor before final print use. 2. NAME RULES (apply everywhere): always lowercase "scoup.ai" in running text, never "Scoup.ai", "SCOUP.AI", "Scoup AI" or "Scoup"; don't start a sentence with it if avoidable (rephrase) — if unavoidable keep lowercase; possessive as "scoup.ai's". Don't put the name in all-caps CSS (text-transform) contexts. The logo image replaces the text name in headers; the text name still appears in titles, alt text, footers, legal text. 3. Marketing site (marketing/site — pages/, static/, build.mjs, test.mjs): header + footer lockup (inline SVG or to a static brand file with alt="scoup.ai", height ≥20px, link to home with accessible name "scoup.ai home"); dark-surface sections use the on-dark files; favicon (favicon.svg + a PNG/ICO fallback only if build supports it — no new deps); pattern "Page – scoup.ai" and home "scoup.ai – Freight invoice audit and overcharge recovery" (adapt to existing copy); og:site_name/og:title/twitter tags; JSON-LD Organization name if present; replace all ~51 "Freight Recovery" brand uses. KEEP descriptive lowercase phrases like "freight invoice recovery"/"freight audit" in body copy for SEO — only the product NAME changes. Legal pages: replace the product name, but DO NOT invent a legal entity name, address or org number — if the pages name a company/legal entity, keep a clearly marked placeholder like "[legal entity name]" and list it in your report. DOMAIN: if canonical URLs, sitemap base, contact emails or CSP reference a domain, switch them to scoup.ai ONLY if the site's base URL is a single config value; otherwise list each occurrence in the report and leave unchanged (the user must confirm they own the domain/mailboxes). Check the site's CSP (_headers) still allows the logo (self-hosted, no inline-style issues). Rebuild dist with the site's build script and run its test.mjs. 4. Web app (web/): index.html <title>scoup.ai + favicon link (copy favicon.svg into web/public), AppShell sidebar lockup (horizontal lockup; optional small descriptor line "Freight invoice recovery" under it in --color-text-subtle, removable), AuthLayout (login/MFA/recovery pages: stacked or horizontal lockup centered), any per-route document titles ("Claims – scoup.ai"), any other user-visible "Freight Recovery" strings (grep web/src, packages/shared user-facing strings, emails/letter templates in api that users or recipients see — e.g. demand letter footer — report each).
